findings.title: Southern Company detects unauthorized access to customer accounts
findings.summary_md: Birmingham NBC affiliate WVTM13 carried Southern Company's disclosure that an unauthorized third party accessed limited information about the accounts of approximately 400,000 customers through the online customer portal. The company said it took immediate steps to stop the activity upon detection and engaged law enforcement. This is the earliest coverage found in this backfill, two days before the story's first_seen timestamp.

findings.title: Southern Company hit by data breach
findings.summary_md: Mobile, Alabama station WALA reported the breach impacted about 400,000 electric customers and detailed the exposed fields: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, and the last four digits of Social Security numbers or business tax IDs. It stated no full Social Security numbers, bank account numbers, credit or debit card numbers, or driver's license numbers were involved, and that Southern Company found no evidence of ongoing unauthorized access.

findings.title: 100,000 Alabama Power Customers Affected in Southern Company Data Breach
findings.summary_md: Birmingham station WBMA reported roughly 100,000 of Alabama Power's 1.6 million customers were affected, with the remaining approximately 300,000 at Georgia Power, which serves about 2.8 million customers. Affected customers are notified by U.S. mail and email and offered one year of free credit monitoring through Equifax. The company said its investigation has not identified evidence of ongoing unauthorized access.

findings.title: Data Breach Affects Alabama Power and Georgia Power Customers
findings.summary_md: Northwest Georgia outlet WEIS reported the notices also identify affected accounts at Mississippi Power and that neither utility's notice specifies when the unauthorized access occurred. Both utilities list 1-800-900-6021 as a dedicated assistance line available weekdays, and the notices explain enrollment in free credit monitoring through Equifax.
